# SOP-P3-L1-05 Planned shutdown - Hot Forge line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03  
Related documents: MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, SB-1033, SB-1044

Purpose
This standard operating procedure (SOP) defines the steps required to perform a planned shutdown of the Hot Forge line at P3-L1. It covers isolation, depressurization, mechanical and electrical lockout, and required inspections for EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03. The procedure is intended to reduce risk during maintenance and to produce records suitable for compliance and maintenance planning.

Background and rationale
Planned shutdowns are controlled events to allow inspection, maintenance, and repairs on the forging line. All mechanical fastening, hydraulic system integrity, and safety interlocks must be verified when components are exposed for work. Specific critical values for the hydraulic press are noted below and must be observed during the shutdown and pre-start sequence to prevent damage and ensure personnel safety.

Critical values
- The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m.
- The system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before initiating step sequence)
1. Maintenance work order issued and approved by line supervisor.
2. A completed risk assessment covering thermal, hydraulic, mechanical, and energy isolation hazards is attached to the work order.
3. Required spare parts and consumables identified on the work order are staged and accessible.
4. A responsible equipment owner is assigned and present during shutdown and startup activities.
5. All operators and maintenance personnel have read this SOP and the referenced documents MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, SB-1033, and SB-1044.

Required PPE
1. Flame-resistant coveralls.
2. Safety glasses with side shields.
3. Cut-resistant gloves for mechanical tasks; insulated gloves for electrical work when electrical energy is present.
4. Steel-toe boots.
5. Hearing protection while in the active line area until the line is verified de-energized.
6. Face shield when performing any press disassembly or when pressurized components are exposed.

Sequence of steps (numbered actions)
1. Notify affected personnel and control room. Post a shutdown notice at the line control station and all access points. Confirm notification is acknowledged by control room operator.
2. Verify that the maintenance work order and attached risk assessment are present at the job site and that all attendees have signed the job briefing.
3. Stop production feed to EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and secure incoming material conveyors. Confirm material is removed from the immediate work area.
4. Isolate energy sources:
   4.1. Lock out and tag out electrical supplies feeding the Hot Forge line per site lockout policy. Ensure the electrical disconnects are physically opened and locked.  
   4.2. Isolate hydraulic power to EQ-P3-L1-HP01, confirm hydraulic control valves are in the closed position, and place locks on the hydraulic pump motor starter.  
   4.3. Bleed hydraulic pressure from the press circuit using the manufacturer’s bleed ports and return lines into an approved reservoir, observing the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar during the bleeding operation.  
   4.4. Verify pneumatic and other utilities are isolated and tagged.
5. Verify zero energy state:
   5.1. Attempt start via main control to verify inability to energize; do not operate any controls while personnel are in the danger area.  
   5.2. Use pressure gauges and indicator lights to confirm zero hydraulic pressure at the press.  
   5.3. Ground any stored energy components per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
6. Drain and secure fluids:
   6.1. Drain die cooling lines and hot-oil circuits where required into approved containers.  
   6.2. Label and contain drained fluids in accordance with SB-1033 and SB-1044.
7. Mechanical isolation and access:
   7.1. Remove guards and access panels only after zero energy is confirmed and locks are in place.  
   7.2. Support heavy assemblies with appropriate mechanical supports before unfastening. Verify support stability throughout the activity.
8. Critical fastener and component checks:
   8.1. When reassembling the press, verify the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Document torque readings in the job record.  
   8.2. Inspect hydraulic hoses, fittings, and seals for wear and replace per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
9. Inspections and repairs:
   9.1. Perform visual and dimensional checks on die faces, ram guides, and bolster surfaces. Record findings on the maintenance checklist.  
   9.2. Replace worn components and document part identifiers in the work order; reference SB-1033 and SB-1044 for cleaning and disposal of removed items.
10. Pre-start verification:
   10.1. Reinstall guards and verify all tools and loose items are removed from the work area.  
   10.2. Remove mechanical supports only after hydraulic pressure is restored and components are confirmed secured.  
   10.3. Restore hydraulic fluid to system and bring pressure up while monitoring for leaks; ensure the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is not exceeded during this step.
11. Functional test:
   11.1. Conduct single-stroke tests at reduced control settings while maintaining visual observation from a safe distance. Confirm correct operation and absence of abnormal noise or leaks before returning to full production control.
12. Return to service:
   12.1. Remove lockout/tagout devices in accordance with the site lockout policy after all personnel have cleared the area and the equipment owner approves restoration.  
   12.2. Complete the work order, attach inspection records, torque logs, and any deviation notes.

Records to keep
1. Completed work order with signatures of the responsible equipment owner and line supervisor.
2. Torque log recording the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) as 1425 N·m and the technician who performed the torqueing.
3. Pressure verification log showing pressures observed during bleed and restart operations; attach any abnormality reports.
4. Visual inspection checklist and photos of critical components, stored per document SB-1033.
5. Fluid handling and disposal records referenced to SB-1044.

Examples and notes
- Example entry for torque log: Component: Ram main bolt; Value: 1425 N·m; Technician: [name]; Date: [job date].  
- If a pressure gauge indicates a trapped pocket above the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is present, stop and re-bleed per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.

Sign-off
1. Equipment owner: name, signature, date.
2. Line supervisor: name, signature, date.
3. Maintenance planner: name, signature, date.
4. Final start permit authorized by control room operator per site procedures.

Referenced documents
- MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1
- SB-1033
- SB-1044
